title: Focus and selection differ
hook: The active panel and the selected item are separate pieces of state.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that a command affects the selected item, which can differ from the panel that has focus

misconception: A command acts on whichever panel you clicked last.
objective: Distinguish choosing a target from bringing a panel into focus.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: The active panel and the selected item are separate pieces of state. Which identifies the item the command will affect here? Correct option: Selection. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The fixture records focus and selection separately. A command target requires inspecting the selected item; shortcuts and focus behaviour vary between applications.
claims.source: Derivation from the explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and transformations in src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts; app documentation below provides command/filter context, not evidence of productivity gains or of every fixture-specific choice. Microsoft Learn, Keyboard accelerators, Common Keyboard Accelerators and scope caveats; retrieved 2026-10-13: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/input/keyboard-accelerators . Shortcuts depend on app, platform and locale; this exercise models the command, not a global keyboard binding. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD UNVERIFIED. Fixture half holds: editResult records focus ('left' → 'right' after Focus right) and selection ('A' → 'B' after Select B) as separate fields, and the stage shows both. The last clause ('shortcuts and focus behaviour vary between applications') is a real-world claim resting on Microsoft Learn (keyboard accelerators), which could not be opened (DNS failure, proxy 403). Left unverified. Options: open the source, or mark that clause as a hedge by ruling. | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Fixture half: studyModels.ts sets focus ('left' -> 'right' after Focus right) and selection ('A' -> 'B' after Select B) as separate fields. Real-world half, on the cited Microsoft Learn page via its GitHub source (raw GitHub MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs, hub/apps/develop/input/keyboard-accelerators.md, opened 2026-10-14). It separates control accelerators, which run 'only if the focus is on the element', from app accelerators that each app defines. It describes scoped and app-wide accelerators, and says that with a TextBox focused 'Control+C ... only copies the currently selected text'. So shortcuts and focus behaviour depend on the application.

claims.text: Every displayed result is computed from the visible exercise state: edit. Local command model; app and locale can differ. The reveal reports this same state and never translates its score into a personal productivity or memory benefit.

recall.question: A is selected in the left panel. You click into the right panel, which holds B, without selecting anything. In this lesson's model, what decides a command's target?
recall.why: Focus and selection are separate state; the target is the selected item. Real apps differ in how focus and shortcuts behave.
